newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Accumulate Indian shares - Caspian.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Accumulate Indian shares - Caspian.

text.p: Investors must see falling Indian share prices as an opportunity to pick up stocks, Caspian Research India Pvt Ltd said.
"The volatility of the next four to five months should be viewed as opportunity to accumulate stock," the securities firm said in its latest report.
The fall in share prices is a logical correction after the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange index had soared 60 percent from a three-year low reached in December 1996, it said.

"Until the end of calendar 1997, we expect sporadic slumps ... driven by concerns over political uncertainty, the risk of a later-than-anticipated economic upturn and expected poor corporate results for the six months to September 30," it said.
In early afternoon trade on Tuesday the BSE index was down 140.20 points, or 3.2 percent, at 4,181.77. It had hit a 34-month high of 4,605.41 more than two weeks ago.

These downswings will be offset by sharp rallies on better liquidity in the economy driving domestic institutional demand, the report prepared by research head Tony Tassell and strategist Chetan Ahya said.
"The net result will be a choppy uptrend until the end of calendar 1997," they said, adding a clearer uptrend will emerge at the start of 1998.
Expectations of strong corporate earnings growth in fiscal 1998/99 (April-March) and statistical evidence of long-delayed pick-up in current sluggish economic evidence will boost the market.
"Overall, we expect the BSE 30 Index to rise to about 4,800 by the fiscal year-end on March 31 (1998)," the report said.
It said the gains would be more if foreign portfolio inflows rise, especially with new allocations for 1998.
